questions.stem: Ceramics is the art and science of making objects from
options: clay and other earthy materials hardened by heat
questions.explanation: Ceramic objects are formed from clay-based materials and fired.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a ceramic product?
questions.explanation: Tiles, bricks, sanitary wares and pots are ceramic products.

questions.stem: The renowned Nigerian potter whose portrait appears on the ₦20 note is
questions.explanation: Ladi Kwali, a Gbari potter trained at the Abuja Pottery Training Centre, is shown on the ₦20 note.

questions.stem: Clay that is found at the site of its parent rock, such as kaolin, is called
questions.explanation: Primary clays remain where they formed; secondary clays are transported and deposited elsewhere.

questions.stem: A fine-grained, highly plastic secondary clay often added to bodies to improve workability is
questions.explanation: Ball clay is very plastic and fine.

questions.stem: Kneading clay to remove air bubbles and make it uniform in texture is called
questions.explanation: Wedging prevents air pockets that can cause bursting in the kiln.

Grog is added to a clay body in order to
options: reduce shrinkage and improve resistance to cracking
questions.explanation: Grog (ground fired clay) opens the body and reduces shrinkage and warping.

questions.stem: A glaze is
options: a thin glassy coating fused to the surface of ceramic ware
questions.explanation: Glaze is glass melted onto the ware.

questions.stem: Cobalt oxide added to a glaze produces a
questions.explanation: Cobalt is a strong blue colourant.

questions.stem: In a glaze, the main glass-forming material is
questions.explanation: Silica forms the glass; fluxes lower its melting point; alumina stiffens it.

questions.stem: Tin oxide is added to a glaze mainly as
options: a flux to lower the melting point
an opacifier to make it white and opaque
questions.explanation: Tin and zirconium oxides make glazes opaque white.

questions.stem: The wire used by potters to separate a thrown pot from the wheel head is a
questions.explanation: A twisted wire with handles cuts clay cleanly.

questions.stem: The furnace in which pottery is fired is the
questions.explanation: Kilns reach the high temperatures needed to fire clay.

questions.stem: The machine that mixes and de-airs plastic clay and extrudes it in a solid column is the
questions.explanation: A pug mill (especially de-airing) produces uniform clay.

questions.stem: A ball mill is used in a ceramic workshop to
options: grind glaze materials finely with water
questions.explanation: Rotating jars with pebbles or balls grind materials.

questions.stem: Small pointed supports placed under glazed ware in the kiln to stop it sticking to the shelf are
questions.explanation: Stilts lift glazed wares; props support shelves; saggars enclose wares.

questions.stem: Before producing a set of mugs, a potter makes a working drawing mainly to
options: plan the shape, proportions and dimensions
questions.explanation: Working drawings guide size and form.

questions.explanation: Coils are joined and smoothed to build walls.

questions.explanation: Clay must be centred before opening and lifting.

questions.stem: Plaster of Paris moulds are used for slip casting because plaster
options: absorbs water from the slip, forming a clay layer on the mould wall
questions.explanation: Porous plaster draws water out of the slip.

questions.explanation: Turning removes excess clay and refines the base.

questions.stem: Polishing leather-hard clay with a smooth pebble or spoon to give it a shine is
questions.explanation: Burnishing compacts the surface to a sheen without glaze.

questions.stem: Scratching through a layer of coloured slip to reveal the clay body underneath is
questions.explanation: Sgraffito ("scratched") exposes the contrasting body.

questions.stem: Applying small separately moulded relief decorations onto the surface of a pot is called
questions.explanation: Sprigs are pressed in moulds and attached with slip.

questions.stem: The first firing of unglazed clay ware is called
questions.explanation: Glost firing is the glaze firing.

questions.stem: Pyrometric cones placed in a kiln are used to
options: indicate the heat work reached during firing
questions.explanation: Cones bend at known combinations of temperature and time.

questions.stem: Fine cracks in a glaze surface caused by the glaze contracting more than the clay body on cooling is
questions.explanation: Crazing results from glaze-body thermal mismatch.

questions.stem: Bare patches where glaze has rolled back from the surface after firing, often due to dust or grease on the bisque, is
questions.explanation: Crawling occurs when glaze does not adhere properly.

questions.topic: Factors in establishing a ceramic industry
questions.stem: An important factor in siting a ceramic factory is
options: nearness to sources of suitable clay and other raw materials
questions.explanation: Raw materials, water, power, transport and market influence location.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, a small ceramic business is registered as a business name with the
questions.explanation: The CAC registers businesses and companies.

questions.topic: Ceramic Production and Sustainable Environmental Issues
questions.stem: Insulating a kiln properly contributes to sustainability mainly by
options: speeding up drying of clay pits
questions.explanation: Insulation reduces heat loss and fuel use.

questions.stem: Potters should wear dust masks when mixing dry clay and glaze materials to avoid
options: inhaling silica dust that damages the lungs
questions.explanation: Silica dust can cause silicosis.

questions.stem: Glazes containing raw lead should not be used on food and drink containers because
options: lead makes the glaze too blue
lead can leach into food and cause poisoning
questions.explanation: Lead is toxic and can dissolve in acidic food.

questions.stem: A museum is an institution that
options: collects, preserves, studies and displays objects of historical, cultural or scientific value
questions.explanation: Museums collect, conserve, research and exhibit artefacts.

questions.stem: The person in charge of the collections of a museum is the
questions.explanation: Curators manage and interpret collections.

questions.stem: The federal body responsible for museums and monuments in Nigeria is the
options: National Commission for Museums and Monuments
questions.explanation: NCMM administers national museums and monuments.

questions.stem:
(a) Define clay. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between primary and secondary clays, giving one example of each. [6 marks]
(c) A test bar of plastic clay measures 15 cm. After drying and firing it measures 13.5 cm. Calculate the total shrinkage as a percentage. [3 marks]
(d) State two reasons for testing clay before use. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Clay: a fine-grained natural earthy material (hydrated aluminium silicate) formed by weathering of feldspathic rocks, plastic when wet and hard when fired
3 marks: Primary/residual clay: found at site of parent rock; coarse, white, less plastic, high firing; e.g. kaolin (china clay)
3 marks: Secondary/sedimentary clay: transported by water, wind or ice and deposited elsewhere; finer, more plastic, often coloured by impurities; e.g. ball clay, fireclay, earthenware clay
3 marks: Shrinkage = (15 - 13.5)/15 x 100 = 10%
4 marks: Any two (2 each): to know plasticity/workability; to know shrinkage for sizing; to know firing temperature/maturity; to detect impurities; to determine colour after firing; to decide suitable products
questions.explanation: Clay is a weathered hydrated aluminium silicate, plastic when wet and hard when fired. Primary clay (kaolin) stays at its source; secondary clay (ball clay) is transported and finer. Shrinkage = 1.5/15 x 100 = 10%. Testing shows plasticity, shrinkage and firing behaviour.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three basic components of a glaze and state the function of each. [6 marks]
(b) State the colour produced by each of the following oxides in an oxidising firing: (i) cobalt oxide; (ii) copper oxide; (iii) iron oxide. [3 marks]
(c) Describe three methods of applying glaze to bisque ware. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Silica: glass former
2 marks: Flux (e.g. feldspar, whiting, borax, soda): lowers the melting point of silica
2 marks: Alumina (from clay/kaolin): stabiliser that stiffens the glaze and prevents running
1 mark: Cobalt: blue
1 mark: Copper: green
1 mark: Iron: brown/amber/honey (accept yellow-brown)
6 marks: Any three described (2 each): dipping - ware immersed in glaze bucket briefly; pouring - glaze poured inside/over ware; spraying - glaze sprayed with gun in spray booth; brushing - glaze painted on with brush
questions.explanation: Glaze = silica (glass), flux (melting) and alumina (stiffener). Cobalt gives blue, copper green, iron brown. Apply by dipping, pouring, spraying or brushing.

questions.topic: Hand building, wheel work and casting
questions.stem: Describe the stages involved in producing a bowl on the potter's wheel, from prepared clay to a leather-hard bowl with a foot ring. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Wedge the clay to remove air and make it uniform; form into a ball
3 marks: Centring: place clay firmly on the wheel head, wet and press with hands while wheel spins until clay runs true
2 marks: Opening: press thumbs into centre to make a hole, leaving adequate base thickness, and widen
3 marks: Pulling/lifting the walls: squeeze clay between fingers inside and outside to raise the walls evenly
2 marks: Shaping: belly out the form, compress and smooth rim and surface with rib/kidney and sponge
1 mark: Cut off with cutting wire and remove onto a bat
2 marks: Allow to dry to leather-hard, invert and turn (trim) to form a foot ring with turning tools
questions.explanation: Wedge, centre, open, pull up walls, shape and smooth, cut off with wire, dry to leather-hard, then invert and turn a foot ring.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the difference between bisque firing and glost firing. [4 marks]
(b) Name four items of kiln furniture and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(c) State three precautions to take when loading a kiln for bisque firing. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Bisque firing: first firing of unglazed, bone-dry ware (about 900-1000 °C) to make it hard and porous for glazing
2 marks: Glost firing: second firing to melt the glaze onto the bisque ware, usually at a higher temperature
8 marks: Any four with use (2 each): kiln shelves/bats - support ware in layers; props/posts - support shelves; stilts/spurs - lift glazed ware off shelves; saggars - protect ware from flames/ash; cones - indicate heat work; setters - support flat ware
3 marks: Any three (1 each): ware must be bone dry; unglazed ware may touch or be stacked; heavier ware at the bottom; allow space for air circulation; do not block spyholes/flues; place cones where visible
questions.explanation: Bisque firing hardens raw ware; glost firing fuses glaze. Kiln furniture: shelves, props, stilts, saggars, cones. Load bone-dry ware, heavier pieces low, leave air space and keep spyholes clear.

questions.stem: Describe how each of the following decorative techniques is carried out, stating the condition of the clay at which it is done: (a) sgraffito; (b) slip trailing; (c) incision; (d) burnishing; (e) stamping (impressing). [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Sgraffito: coat leather-hard ware with contrasting slip; scratch through slip to reveal body (leather-hard)
3 marks: Slip trailing: squeeze slip from a trailer/bulb in lines or dots onto the surface (soft to leather-hard)
3 marks: Incision: cut or carve lines into the surface with a pointed tool (leather-hard)
3 marks: Burnishing: rub surface with smooth pebble, spoon or bone to compact and polish (leather-hard to nearly dry)
3 marks: Stamping/impressing: press carved stamps, roulettes, seeds or objects into soft clay (plastic/soft leather-hard)
questions.explanation: Sgraffito scratches through slip; slip trailing pipes slip lines; incision cuts lines; burnishing polishes with a pebble; stamping impresses patterns. Most are done at leather-hard; stamping is on softer clay.

questions.stem:
(a) State five functions of a museum. [5 marks]
(b) Distinguish between a museum and an art gallery. [4 marks]
(c) Explain three ways in which museums contribute to the economy of a country. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: Any five (1 each): collection of artefacts; preservation/conservation; research; documentation; exhibition/display; education of the public; promotion of cultural heritage
4 marks: Museum: collects and preserves artefacts of historical, cultural or scientific value, mainly not for sale (2); art gallery: displays works of art, often contemporary, which may be for sale (2)
6 marks: Any three explained (2 each): tourism and foreign exchange; employment of staff; revenue from fees and shops; encourages crafts and local industry; research that supports creative industries
questions.explanation: Museums collect, conserve, research, document, exhibit and educate. Museums preserve heritage collections; galleries display (often sell) artworks. Museums boost tourism, jobs and revenue.
